title: Cabbage and cheddar pasta with crispy sage

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain kitchen staple: butter, cabbage, onion, garlic, dried pasta, crème fraîche, cheddar, sage and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Everything is an everyday item at any Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a frying pan, a colander and a grater, and the techniques are simple frying and boiling.

works.reason: Half a cabbage, 350g pasta, 120g cheddar and crème fraîche loosened with pasta water make a well-balanced, well-seasoned dish for four, and the 15-minute fry will soften and colour the cabbage.

honest_times.reason: Shredding half a cabbage, slicing an onion and garlic, and grating cheese fit in 15 minutes, and the 15-minute cabbage fry runs alongside the pasta, which suits a quick dinner.

honest_ingredients.reason: Penne is dried pasta and every listed item, including the sage and the lemon (used as zest), appears in the steps, with nothing unlisted apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Slow-fried white cabbage is the bulk and point of this warming pasta, which suits a chilly late-March evening.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a satisfying family pasta with plenty of cabbage and onion alongside cheese for protein.
